assumptions: Impulsive burn of the TARGET along its along-track (T) axis; dv > 0 = posigrade.
Clohessy-Wiltshire displacement on a circular reference orbit (mean motion from t_j2k_sma), read curvilinearly (radius difference, arc length) in the local RTN frame at the new TCA.
Covariance, relative velocity and HBR unchanged by the burn (covariances stay attached to each object's local RTN frame); the TCA shift is handled by projecting onto the encounter plane.
Target eccentricity: its true anomaly is not in the CDM, so an along-track shift dT moves the target by up to +-e|dT| radially; robust mode takes the worst case over that interval.

Execution / model scale error: robust mode requires the Pc target for burn magnitudes within +-execution_error of the recommendation (this envelope also covers the CW scale errors from eccentricity, <= 3.8 %, and J2, <= 0.45 %), plus model_margin_decades of Pc.
J2 is not modelled (<= 0.012 decades of Pc measured end-to-end).

Sign convention: relative_position / relative_velocity = chaser - target (CCSDS: object 2 - object 1). Verified for the velocity (energy relation); the position sign cannot be verified from the dataset (Pc, Mahalanobis and miss distance are sign-blind). If it were reversed, the posigrade / retrograde choice would flip - both directions are always returned under 'options'.
No check of new conjunctions with other objects or of the post-burn orbit.

hbr_modes.auto: radius solved per CDM from ESA's max_risk_estimate: calibrated on an ESA output, so its agreement with ESA risk is partly circular. Label results 'radius calibrated on ESA'.
hbr_modes.spans: (t_span + c_span) / 2 from the CDM inputs only: the independent reproduction of ESA risk.
